question: What is the meaning of recycling efficiency for producing feedstock in relation to sustainability properties?
description: The recycling efficiency for producing feedstock is defined as the ratio of the mass of output fractions accounting for recycling by the mass of the waste input fraction expressed as a percentage. This definition supports the assessment of sustainability properties in circular construction, as it evaluates the effectiveness of recycling processes in reducing waste and conserving resources. The recycling efficiency value can be used to understand the quality of recycling and its impact on circularity, as it takes into account the mass of waste generated during the recycling process. In the context of the Madaster platform, this definition is applied to calculate the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI), which is a key indicator of sustainability properties in circular construction. The MCI is calculated as 1 minus the Linear Flow Index (LFI) multiplied by the product utility (F(X)), where F(X) represents the maximization of the usefulness and lifespan of a product to reduce waste and resource consumption. The LFI is calculated as the sum of the total mass of virgin feedstock (V) and the mass of unrecoverable waste (W) divided by twice the mass of the product (M).
